mica: Heads-up: onboarding run for nova-15B-int4 shows progressive checksum drift in KV checks after token ~4300. noticed while validating long-doc summarization suite.

mica: Quick summary: baseline fp16/int8 stable. int4 diverges, and kv-checksum in the tracer toggles between two values every ~1024 tokens.

devon: can you drop the small trace? i want to see the raw per-shard position math.

mica: pasted snippet below (trimmed):
```
TRACE: token=4299 shard=0 pos_global=4299 pos_shard=1023 checksum=0x9a3f
TRACE: token=4300 shard=0 pos_global=4300 pos_shard=1024 checksum=0x9a3f
TRACE: token=4301 shard=1 pos_global=4301 pos_shard=0    checksum=0x4b2c <-- flips here
TRACE: token=4302 shard=1 pos_global=4302 pos_shard=1    checksum=0x4b2c
```

jen: shard wrap at 1024? our standard shard size is 2048 for this config, right? looks like a half-shard wrap.

mica: correct, we expect pos_shard to continue to 2047 then wrap. so pos_shard hitting 0 at 4301 implies an unexpected division by 2 somewhere.

devon: thought: in the int4 packer we changed the packing stride to pack two tokens per byte for keys and made an optimization to compute shard_offset = (global_pos / stride) % shard_len. if stride got mixed up (used old_stride vs new_stride) you get a factor-of-2.

mica: i instrumented the packer and saw packer.stride == 2 but the recompute path used stride == 1. added an assert and it trips during eviction recompute.

ops-bot: NOTE: recent deploy tagged model/nova-15b-int4 v2026-03-15 included quant-packer micro-optimizations.

jen: that would align with regression window. Did we run an explicit prefill-long test for nova? not yet i think.

mica: no, we didn't. onboarding CI had only up-to-3k tests. adding 8k prefill test now.

devon: low-risk mitigation: introduce a runtime guard that rewrites model-profile to prefer int8 for requests when max_context > 4096 until int4 validated. we can push as traffic-routing flag.

mica: agreed. also added a unit test: tests/test_packer_stride.py with 3 cases covering stride=1/2/4 and eviction recompute. failing case reproduced locally.

mica: on it. fuzz harness added as tools/prefill_fuzz.py and a job in ci:prefill-fuzz (short).

devon: for root cause notes: i opened ticket ML-2304 (int4 packer stride mismatch) and ML-2305 (eviction-recompute stride inconsistency). linking both to onboarding.

jen: plan to revert the micro-optimization? or fix in place?

mica: perf note: int4 still gives ~2.3x tokens/sec vs fp16 on hot path. fallback to int8 reduces that to ~1.6x but prevents tail regressions.
